nodes.label: Gemini API selector self-healing
nodes.rationale: CSS selectors on Instacart break as the site changes; instead of hard failure, broken selectors are repaired at runtime via the Gemini API (optional GEMINI_API_KEY), keeping the scraper working without manual selector maintenance. A fixed set of healable selector keys (address_input, product_price, store_card, etc.) bounds what the healer may rewrite, and --heal-only with an --html-file allows offline repair against saved debug HTML.

nodes.label: 3-stage store lookup
nodes.rationale: --stores is not limited to Instacart's visible storefront page. Lookup tries, in order: (1) the visible storefront list, (2) Instacart's own search bar, (3) a direct URL guess. This lets any store that delivers to the address (e.g. Hannaford) be found and searched even when it is absent from the storefront page. Shared by product_search and recipe_scraper via the core module.

nodes.label: Multi-recipe page selection (--recipe flag)
nodes.rationale: Recipe pages are often roundups ('10 best...' lists) containing several recipes. The --recipe flag selects one by number or by name; without it the first recipe is used and the full list of found recipes is printed so the user can re-run with an explicit choice.

nodes.label: Env-driven delivery address (DELIVERY_ADDRESS / --address)
nodes.rationale: The delivery address is no longer hardcoded: it comes from a DELIVERY_ADDRESS variable in the repo-root .env (gitignored), with a --address CLI flag as a one-off override. The same address must be set during the --login browser session so the saved session and env agree.

nodes.label: Full-department crawl with product caps
nodes.rationale: run_scraper scrapes every department by default (150 products per department, 5 stores); --departments narrows to named departments, --max-products caps per department, --max-per-store caps total per store, and --max-stores 0 means every store found. Caps of 0 mean unlimited. Lowering caps and avoiding --headless is also the recommended mitigation for bot-blocking/CAPTCHAs.

nodes.label: Filtered min-max price range per search term
nodes.rationale: Product and ingredient prices are reported as a min-max range across top search matches rather than a single guess; only products whose name actually contains the search terms count toward the range, so searching 'butter' is not skewed by 'butter cookies'. --results widens the range by considering more matches per store.
